name: ossify
description: Skeleton-first lifecycle from Release 0 through MVP and v1. workspace-init is optional - /ossify:start and /ossify:adopt author the topology declaration themselves. Since 1.8.0 /ossify:run-spine accepts an optional --external-executor flag handing the work items of a round to a caller-supplied, provider-neutral in-session procedure; the no-flag command is unchanged. Since 1.14.0 /ossify:run-spine re-enters a started spine on its own, at a round barrier or mid-round, printing a reconcile read-out and halting before any mutation on state it cannot reconcile. Since 1.16.0 a demo line starts planned until its spine builds it, and a spine's own user line can be deferred to a release or closed under a declared escape. Since 1.17.0 an AC can name both halves (`exit <n> and output contains <str>`), an output check never passes a command that cannot run, every prose snippet calls `oss` by name, and work-item asks whether each test can fail.

interface.shortDescription: Plan a release as a skeleton and drive it from Release 0 through MVP and v1.
interface.longDescription: Ossify plans a release as a skeleton, drives its spine round by round, and closes it with a ceremony that harvests what the round learned. workspace-init is optional as of 1.3.0: the first entry point authors .ossify/topology.json itself when nothing resolves on the walk-up path, and reads a workspace-init .workspace/pairing.json as a translated fallback when one exists. The grill and the adversarial critic are internal (the challenge skill) since 1.1.0, so the release-planning veto and the spine-close audit run on every install; an external fresh-frame adversary joins close-depth audits when one is configured. One limit on Codex specifically: round execution dispatches an implementer subagent that only Claude Code registers.
defaultPrompt: Onboard this project's spec core with ossify.
Open the next release and plan its spine.
